answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a refundable bond before it may place orders, then slash that bond when a dispute proves fraud or coordinated abuse. This does not make identities unique; it makes multiplying them costly, because each fresh persona needs separately locked capital and risks losing it. A sonnet-writing bot cannot gain influence merely by spawning an atlas of velvet-named accounts: unless those accounts bring real bonded stake, their votes and trade limits stay small.
